details: The Federal Reserve concluded its June 16-17 meeting, opting to keep interest rates steady within the 3.50%-3.75% range, a widely anticipated decision. Market attention now shifts to the newly released economic projections, especially the "dot plot" which signals future interest rate paths, and the inaugural press conference by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Investors are keenly watching for any hawkish cues in his communication, particularly concerning persistent inflation, as such signals could introduce downward pressure on risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Fed Holds Rates, Market Awaits "Dot Plot" and Warsh's Guidance

details: The US headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) accelerated to 4.2% year-over-year in May, marking its highest level in three years, primarily driven by energy costs. However, the core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices and is a key metric for the Federal Reserve, came in at a more subdued 2.9% year-over-year, falling below forecasts. Bitcoin's immediate reaction to the data was muted, showing a brief dip before recovering, suggesting that markets are looking beyond the headline figure to the less alarming core inflation. This data will continue to influence the Fed's future monetary policy considerations.
title: US May CPI Rises to 4.2%, Core Inflation Muted

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has increased its deposit rate to 2.25% following a surge in eurozone inflation to 3.2%. This move by the ECB indicates a tightening of global liquidity, which generally creates a less favorable environment for speculative assets, including cryptocurrencies, as capital becomes more expensive and risk-free returns become more attractive.
title: ECB Raises Deposit Rate Amid Eurozone Inflation Surge

details: A recent agreement between the US and Iran, aiming to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, has led to a significant drop in oil prices. This de-escalation of geopolitical tensions has triggered a relief rally across various risk assets in global financial markets, including Bitcoin, as concerns over energy-driven inflation have eased.
title: US-Iran Deal Lowers Oil Prices, Boosts Risk Assets

details: After a brief pause, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have once again experienced net outflows, including a notable exit of funds from Grayscale's GBTC. The ongoing nature of these outflows indicates fragile institutional support for Bitcoin and suggests a weakening of a reliable demand floor, potentially contributing to downward pressure on Bitcoin's price.
title: US Spot Bitcoin ETFs See Continued Outflows
